metaTitle: Leaky Faucet Repair in Pasadena, CA | $135–$220
metaDescription: Fix a dripping faucet in your Pasadena home. Flat-rate pricing $135–$220, common in Craftsman and Spanish-revival houses with older plumbing.
intro: That steady drip from your kitchen or bathroom faucet is usually a worn part, not a sign your whole plumbing system is failing. In Pasadena's older Craftsman and Spanish-revival homes, original fixtures and galvanized supply lines mean faucets often need repair sooner than in newer construction. Left alone, a leak can waste water and stain vintage tile or porcelain fixtures that are hard to match today.
causes: A worn rubber washer or O-ring inside the faucet body, common after decades of use in original 1920s-1930s fixtures.
Corroded or mineral-clogged valve seats caused by Pasadena's hard water depositing scale over time.
A failing cartridge in newer replacement faucets installed inside older cabinetry.
Loose packing nuts or a worn stem, often found in homes that still have their original faucet hardware.
Old, brittle supply line connections that have degraded and start leaking at the faucet base.
whatProDoes: Shuts off the water supply and inspects the faucet type to identify whether it's a compression, ball, cartridge, or ceramic disk design.
Disassembles the faucet handle and body to check washers, O-rings, valve seats, and cartridges for wear or mineral buildup.
Replaces the failed part with a compatible component, which can be trickier in older Pasadena homes where original fixtures use discontinued sizes.
Cleans mineral deposits from valve seats and threads to reduce future scale buildup from hard water.
Reassembles the faucet, turns the water back on, and checks for leaks at the handle, spout, and base connections.
diyOrPro: If you're comfortable turning off the water shutoff and don't mind removing a faucet handle, replacing a simple washer can be a reasonable DIY task with the right size part. But if the faucet is original to a 1920s or 1930s Pasadena home, finding matching parts can be difficult, and forcing old, corroded fittings risks cracking porcelain or breaking a shutoff valve that then requires a bigger repair. When in doubt, or if the leak involves the supply lines rather than just the faucet handle, it's worth having a plumber take a look.
priceNote: This repair runs $135 to $220, based on a $94 hourly rate and a typical job length of 1 to 2 hours. Faucets in Pasadena's older homes sometimes take longer because parts for original or vintage fixtures aren't always standard sizes, and mineral buildup from hard water can make disassembly slower.

faqs.q: Why is my faucet still dripping after I tightened the handle?
faqs.a: Tightening the handle can temporarily slow a drip, but if the internal washer, O-ring, or cartridge is worn, the leak will return. The fix requires replacing the worn part, not just tightening what's already there.

faqs.q: Will the plumber be able to find parts for my old faucet?
faqs.a: Many Craftsman and Spanish-revival homes in Pasadena still have original or older-style faucets, and matching replacement parts can take extra time to source or may require a compatible modern equivalent. A plumber can tell you during the visit whether an exact match is available.

faqs.q: Is a dripping faucet actually worth fixing, or can I just ignore it?
faqs.a: A slow drip wastes water and money over time, and in older homes it can also lead to mineral staining on porcelain or tile that's difficult to remove. It's a small repair now compared to dealing with water damage or a bigger valve failure later.
